accuracy.evidence: Group facts checked against the Year 1 programme and standard KS1 references: mammals have hair or fur and feed young milk (whale, bat, dolphin, seal included), birds have feathers, a beak and wings (penguin included), fish have fins and gills with most scaled (shark, goldfish, eel, trout), reptiles have dry scaly skin (snake, crocodile, lizard, tortoise), amphibians have smooth damp skin (frog, toad, newt). No claim that all mammals give live birth or that all fish have scales, so platypus and scaleless fish are not contradicted.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented sorting errors for ages 5-7: grouping by habitat (whale, dolphin as fish), by movement (bat as bird, every bird flies), confusing reptiles and amphibians (lizard versus frog, frog as reptile), thinking snakes are slimy, and treating a shared feature (fins, living in the sea) as a reason to separate two animals. Each is a prediction distractor, a canvas voice line or a tagged challenge slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built for this topic: coverings drawn as fur, feather, scale and damp-skin swatches, a drag-to-group sort with the whale, bat and penguin traps, a build-an-animal figure that grows a beak, wings, fins, gills or a coat as parts are chosen, an odd-one-out row and a which-clue-separates-them chooser. It passed the 30% shingle gate against every flag lab, including flag_plant and the existing sorting labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child first notices what covers each animal, then uses that covering to sort, then meets animals whose home or movement misleads, then builds each group from its defining parts, then spots the animal from a different group, and finally learns that a good clue is true for one animal and not the other. Success lines restate the rule, e.g. 'A whale and a bat are mammals. A penguin is a bird.'

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: what covers a snake ('Slime' tempts), which group a whale is in ('Fish' tempts because it lives in the sea), which part every bird has ('Fur' and 'Fins' check the defining feature), and which of goldfish, shark and dolphin is not a fish ('Shark' tempts because it looks fierce). The reveal line reports the child's guess against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions with fourteen tagged slips (fly, batrep, lizard, water, fur, scales, sea, amph, frogrep, eel, allfly, pengfish, dolph, both). Each message names the misleading clue and gives the body feature that decides, e.g. 'Living in the sea does not make a fish. A whale breathes air and feeds its babies milk: a mammal.'

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 1.1 (family kid limit 5.0) in short sentences about fur, feathers and skin; adult text scores 8.5 (limit 10.0) and uses vertebrate, mammal, amphibian, reptile, gills and external structure with the curriculum wording. The young class gives 56 px buttons, emoji pictures carry every animal, and on-canvas prompts are one short line.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler scan and the 12% explanation-overlap gate; the nearest lessons (174 Animals and their babies, 390 Where animals live and 497 Herbivores, carnivores and omnivores) do not share wording. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (coverings, the five groups, tricky mammals, the penguin and body-not-home) and the adult paragraphs cover standards, definitions, named mistakes and the lab.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px and iPhone 13 in light and dark, before, during and after Show me for every step: coat tiles sit in a 2 x 2 block with swatches, the five group bins sit 3 + 2 below a large draggable emoji, part cards are a 2 x 3 block, the odd-one-out cards fill the width, and each finished step shows a summary picture instead of an empty canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations and no console errors. Every drag or canvas tap has a labelled button twin (the four coverings, the five groups, the six parts, the three animals by name, the three clues) and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each spoken line, so the emoji pictures are never the only cue.
